newsitem.title: ITALY: Arbiter to issue ruling on disputed Bosnian town.
newsitem.headline: Arbiter to issue ruling on disputed Bosnian town.

text.p: An American arbiter will announce his decision in Rome on Friday on whether Serbs or Moslems should control the strategic town of Brcko in northern Bosnia, diplomatic sources said on Wednesday.

They said the arbiter, lawyer Roberts Owen, would make his announcement in the presence of members of the international Contact Group for former Yugoslavia and the international community's High Representative for Bosnia, Carl Bildt.
The dispute over the narrow Brcko land corridor, which links eastern and western halves of Bosnian Serb-controlled territory, nearly caused talks on ending Bosnia's war to collapse in November 1995.
February 15 is the deadline for settlement of the dispute.
Serb and Moslem delegations presented their arguments during 10 days of arbitration hearings in Rome last month.

The Bosnian Serbs, who seized Brcko early in the 1992-95 war, insist that the town must be kept under Serb control or Serb territory would be cut in half. They have threatened to go to war over the issue.
Moslem leaders say Brcko should be awarded to the Moslem- Croat federation based on the pre-war population in which Moslems and Croats formed a majority.
They say giving the Sava river port to the Serbs would reward ethnic expulsions carried out when Serb forces captured the area in May 1992.
